/**
 * Handles the acceptance of a new connection.
 *
 * @param key The selection key associated with the server socket channel.
 * @param i The iterator over the selection keys.
 * @throws IOException If an I/O error occurs.
 * @throws InterruptedException If the thread is interrupted.
 */
private void doAccept(SelectionKey key, Iterator<SelectionKey> i) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
    if (!onConnect(key)) {
        key.cancel();
        return;
    }
    SocketChannel channel = server.accept();
    if (channel == null) {
        return;
    }
    channel.configureBlocking(false);
    Socket socket = channel.socket();
    socket.setTcpNoDelay(isTcpNoDelay());
    socket.setKeepAlive(true);
    WebSocketImpl w = wsf.createWebSocket(this, drafts);
    w.setSelectionKey(channel.register(selector, SelectionKey.OP_READ, w));
    try {
        w.setChannel(wsf.wrapChannel(channel, w.getSelectionKey()));
        i.remove();
        allocateBuffers(w);
    } catch (IOException ex) {
        if (w.getSelectionKey() != null) {
            w.getSelectionKey().cancel();
        }
        handleIOException(w.getSelectionKey(), null, ex);
    }
}
```
508	```java
/**
 * Reads data from a WebSocket connection.
 *
 * @param key The SelectionKey associated with the WebSocket connection.
 * @param i The Iterator over SelectionKeys.
 * @return true if the read operation was successful, false otherwise.
 * @throws InterruptedException if the thread is interrupted.
 * @throws IOException if an I/O error occurs.
 */
private boolean doRead(SelectionKey key, Iterator<SelectionKey> i) throws InterruptedException, IOException {
    WebSocketImpl conn = (WebSocketImpl) key.attachment();
    ByteBuffer buf = takeBuffer();
    if (conn.getChannel() == null) {
        key.cancel();
        handleIOException(key, conn, new IOException());
        return false;
    }
    try {
        if (SocketChannelIOHelper.read(buf, conn, conn.getChannel())) {
            if (buf.hasRemaining()) {
                conn.inQueue.put(buf);
                queue(conn);
                i.remove();
                if (conn.getChannel() instanceof WrappedByteChannel && ((WrappedByteChannel) conn.getChannel()).isNeedRead()) {
                    iqueue.add(conn);
                }
            } else {
                pushBuffer(buf);
            }
        } else {
            pushBuffer(buf);
        }
    } catch (IOException e) {
        pushBuffer(buf);
        throw e;
    }
    return true;
}
```

/**
 * Ensures that the current instance can only be started once.
 * If the instance has already been started, it throws an IllegalStateException.
 * If the instance is closed, it returns false.
 * Otherwise, it sets the current thread as the selector thread and returns true.
 *
 * @return true if the instance can be started, false if it is closed
 */
private boolean doEnsureSingleThread() {
    synchronized (this) {
        if (selectorthread != null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(getClass().getName() + " can only be started once.");
        }
        selectorthread = Thread.currentThread();
        if (isclosed.get()) {
            return false;
        }
    }
    return true;
}

516	```java
/**
 * Broadcasts data to a collection of WebSocket clients.
 * 
 * @param data The data to broadcast, which can be a String or ByteBuffer.
 * @param clients The collection of WebSocket clients to receive the data.
 */
private void doBroadcast(Object data, Collection<WebSocket> clients) {
    String sData = null;
    ByteBuffer bData = null;
    
    // Convert data to appropriate type
    if (data instanceof String) {
        sData = (String) data;
    } else if (data instanceof ByteBuffer) {
        bData = (ByteBuffer) data;
    }
    
    // If no valid data, return
    if (sData == null && bData == null) {
        return;
    }
    
    // Map to hold draft frames for each draft
    Map<Draft, List<Framedata>> draftFrames = new HashMap<>();
    
    // Iterate over each client
    for (WebSocket client : clients) {
        if (client != null) {
            Draft draft = client.getDraft();
            fillFrames(draft, draftFrames, sData, bData);
            
            try {
                // Send frames to the client
                client.sendFrame(draftFrames.get(draft));
            } catch (WebsocketNotConnectedException e) {
                // Ignore this exception
            }
        }
    }
}
```
517	```java
/**
 * Fills the frames for a given draft.
 * 
 * @param draft The draft to fill frames for.
 * @param draftFrames A map to store the draft and its corresponding frames.
 * @param sData A string data to create frames from.
 * @param bData A byte buffer data to create frames from.
 */
private void fillFrames(Draft draft, Map<Draft, List<Framedata>> draftFrames, String sData, ByteBuffer bData) {
    if (!draftFrames.containsKey(draft)) {
        List<Framedata> frames = null;
        if (sData != null) {
            frames = draft.createFrames(sData, false);
        }
        if (bData != null) {
            frames = draft.createFrames(bData, false);
        }
        if (frames != null) {
            draftFrames.put(draft, frames);
        }
    }
}
```
518	### Summary:
The `transferByteBuffer` method transfers data from a source `ByteBuffer` to a destination `ByteBuffer`. It first checks if either buffer is null and throws an `IllegalArgumentException` if so. It then calculates the remaining bytes in both buffers. If the source has more remaining bytes than the destination, it limits the source to the number of bytes the destination can hold and transfers those bytes to the destination. If the source has fewer or equal remaining bytes, it transfers all of them to the destination. The method returns the number of bytes transferred.

538	```java
/**
 * This method handles the execution of a request within a context. It first attempts to retrieve a context from the thread-local storage. If a context is found, it updates the context with the new request and calls itself recursively with the updated context. If no context is found, it creates a new context, updates it with the new request, and calls itself recursively with the new context.
 *
 * @param req The request to be executed.
 * @return A CompletionStage containing the result of the request execution.
 */
public CompletionStage<Result> call(Request req) {
    return Context.safeCurrent()
        .map(threadLocalCtx -> {
            Context newCtx = threadLocalCtx.withRequest(req.removeAttr(CTX_ARGS));
            Context.setCurrent(newCtx);
            return call(newCtx);
        })
        .orElseGet(() -> {
            Context ctx = new Context(req.removeAttr(CTX_ARGS), contextComponents);
            ctx.args = req.attrs().getOptional(CTX_ARGS).orElse(new HashMap<>());
            return call(ctx);
        });
}
```

552	```java
@Override
public CompletionStage<Result> onClientError(RequestHeader request, int statusCode, String message) {
    if (statusCode == 400) {
        return onBadRequest(request, message);
    } else if (statusCode == 403) {
        return onForbidden(request, message);
    } else if (statusCode == 404) {
        return onNotFound(request, message);
    } else if (statusCode >= 400 && statusCode < 500) {
        return onOtherClientError(request, statusCode, message);
    } else {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("onClientError invoked with non client error status code " + statusCode + ": " + message);
    }
}
```

**Summary:**
The `onClientError` method handles different client error status codes by delegating to specific methods (`onBadRequest`, `onForbidden`, `onNotFound`, `onOtherClientError`) based on the `statusCode`. If the `statusCode` is not a client error (i.e., not in the range 400-499), it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`.

588	```java
/**
 * Calculates the relative path from a start path to a target path.
 * 
 * @param startPath The starting path.
 * @param targetPath The target path.
 * @return The relative path from startPath to targetPath.
 */
public static String relative(String startPath, String targetPath) {
    // If the start and target paths are the same, return the current directory.
    if (startPath.equals(targetPath)) {
        return CURRENT_DIR;
    }

    // Convert the start and target paths to canonical form and split them into segments.
    String[] start = toSegments(canonical(startPath));
    String[] target = toSegments(canonical(targetPath));

    // If the start path does not end with a separator, remove the last segment.
    if (!startPath.endsWith(SEPARATOR)) {
        start = Arrays.copyOfRange(start, 0, start.length - 1);
    }

    // If the target path does not end with a separator, remove the last segment and store it.
    String targetFile = "";
    if (!targetPath.endsWith(SEPARATOR)) {
        targetFile = target[target.length - 1];
        target = Arrays.copyOfRange(target, 0, target.length - 1);
    }

    // Find the common prefix between the start and target paths.
    String[] common = commonPrefix(start, target);

    // Calculate the number of parent directories needed to reach the common prefix.
    String[] parents = toParentDirs(start.length - common.length);

    // Calculate the relative path from the common prefix to the target path.
    int relativeStartIdx = common.length;
    String[] relativeDirs = Arrays.copyOfRange(target, relativeStartIdx, target.length);
    String[] relativePath = Arrays.copyOf(parents, parents.length + relativeDirs.length);
    System.arraycopy(relativeDirs, 0, relativePath, parents.length, relativeDirs.length);

    // If the relative path is not empty, add a trailing separator.
    String trailingSep = "";
    if (relativePath.length > 0) {
        trailingSep = SEPARATOR;
    }

    // Join the relative path segments and append the target file.
    return Arrays.stream(relativePath).collect(Collectors.joining(SEPARATOR)) + trailingSep + targetFile;
}
```
589	```java
/**
 * Converts a URL to its canonical form by removing redundant path components.
 * 
 * @param url The URL to be canonicalized.
 * @return The canonicalized URL.
 */
public static String canonical(String url) {
    String[] urlPath = toSegments(url);
    Stack<String> canonical = new Stack<>();
    for (String comp : urlPath) {
        if (comp.isEmpty() || comp.equals(CURRENT_DIR)) continue;
        if (!comp.equals(PARENT_DIR) || (!canonical.empty() && canonical.peek().equals(PARENT_DIR))) {
            canonical.push(comp);
        } else {
            canonical.pop();
        }
    }
    String prefixSep = url.startsWith(SEPARATOR) ? SEPARATOR : "";
    String trailingSep = url.endsWith(SEPARATOR) ? SEPARATOR : "";
    return prefixSep + canonical.stream().collect(Collectors.joining(SEPARATOR)) + trailingSep;
}

/**
 * Retrieves the current EntityManager from the stack.
 * If no EntityManager is found, it throws a RuntimeException with a message
 * suggesting to annotate the action method with @play.db.jpa.Transactional or
 * to wrap the call in JPAApi.withTransaction, or to ensure that the HTTP context is setup.
 * 
 * @return The current EntityManager.
 */
public EntityManager em() {
    Deque<EntityManager> ems = this.emStack(true);
    if (ems.isEmpty()) {
        Http.Context.safeCurrent().map(ctx -> {
            throw new RuntimeException("No EntityManager found in the context. Try to annotate your action method with @play.db.jpa.Transactional");
        }).orElseGet(() -> {
            throw new RuntimeException("No EntityManager bound to this thread. Try wrapping this call in JPAApi.withTransaction, or ensure that the HTTP context is setup on this thread.");
        });
    }
    return ems.peekFirst();
}

public static <In, FlowIn, Out> Flow<In, Out, ?> bypassWith(Function<In, F.Either<FlowIn, Out>> splitter, Flow<FlowIn, Out, ?> flow) {
    return bypassWith(
        Flow.<In>create().map(splitter::apply),
        play.api.libs.streams.AkkaStreams.onlyFirstCanFinishMerge(2),
        flow
    );
}
```

This method `bypassWith` takes two parameters: a `Function<In, F.Either<FlowIn, Out>>` named `splitter` and a `Flow<FlowIn, Out, ?>` named `flow`. It returns a `Flow<In, Out, ?>`. The method uses `Flow.create().map(splitter::apply)` to apply the `splitter` function to each input element, which results in a `F.Either<FlowIn, Out>`. The `onlyFirstCanFinishMerge` method from `play.api.libs.streams.AkkaStreams` is then used to merge the resulting flows, ensuring that only the first one to finish will continue.
625	```java
public static <In, FlowIn, Out> Flow<In, Out, ?> bypassWith(
    Flow<In, F.Either<FlowIn, Out>, ?> splitter,
    Graph<UniformFanInShape<Out, Out>, ?> mergeStrategy,
    Flow<FlowIn, Out, ?> flow) {
    return splitter.via(Flow.fromGraph(GraphDSL.create(builder -> {
        UniformFanOutShape<F.Either<FlowIn, Out>, F.Either<FlowIn, Out>> broadcast = builder.add(Broadcast.create(2, true));
        UniformFanInShape<Out, Out> merge = builder.add(mergeStrategy);
        Flow<F.Either<FlowIn, Out>, FlowIn, ?> collectIn = Flow.create().collect(Scala.partialFunction(x -> {
            if (x.left.isPresent()) {
                return x.left.get();
            } else {
                throw Scala.noMatch();
            }
        }));
        Flow<F.Either<FlowIn, Out>, Out, ?> collectOut = Flow.create().collect(Scala.partialFunction(x -> {
            if (x.right.isPresent()) {
                return x.right.get();
            } else {
                throw Scala.noMatch();
            }
        }));
        Flow<F.Either<FlowIn, Out>, F.Either<FlowIn, Out>, ?> blockCancel = play.api.libs.streams.AkkaStreams.<F.Either<FlowIn, Out>>ignoreAfterCancellation().asJava();

        builder.from(broadcast.out(0)).via(builder.add(collectIn)).via(builder.add(flow)).toInlet(merge.in(0));
        builder.from(broadcast.out(1)).via(builder.add(blockCancel)).via(builder.add(collectOut)).toInlet(merge.in(1));

        return new FlowShape<>(broadcast.in(), merge.out());
    })));
}
```

public <T> String print(TypeDescriptor desc, T t) {
    if (t == null) {
        return "";
    }
    if (desc != null && conversion.canConvert(desc, TypeDescriptor.valueOf(String.class))) {
        return (String) conversion.convert(t, desc, TypeDescriptor.valueOf(String.class));
    } else if (conversion.canConvert(t.getClass(), String.class)) {
        return conversion.convert(t, String.class);
    } else {
        return t.toString();
    }
}
```

If no specific conversion is possible but a conversion from the class of `t` to `String` is possible, it performs that conversion. If neither conversion is possible, it returns the string representation of `t` using `t.toString()`.

/**
 * Registers a converter that handles conversion between `Optional` and `String` types.
 * 
 * <p>The converter performs the following:
 * - Converts from `String` to `Optional` by converting the string to the target type and wrapping it in an `Optional`.
 * - Converts from `Optional` to `String` by converting the contained value to a string if present, or returning an empty string if the `Optional` is empty.
 * 
 * @return The current instance of the `Formatters` class, allowing for method chaining.
 */
private Formatters registerOptional() {
    conversion.addConverter(new GenericConverter() {
        @Override
        public Object convert(Object source, TypeDescriptor sourceType, TypeDescriptor targetType) {
            if (sourceType.getObjectType().equals(String.class)) {
                Object element = conversion.convert(source, sourceType, targetType.elementTypeDescriptor(source));
                return Optional.ofNullable(element);
            } else if (targetType.getObjectType().equals(String.class)) {
                if (source == null) return "";
                Optional<?> opt = (Optional) source;
                return opt.map(o -> conversion.convert(source, sourceType.getElementTypeDescriptor(), targetType)).orElse("");
            }
            return null;
        }

        @Override
        public Set<GenericConverter.ConvertiblePair> getConvertibleTypes() {
            Set<ConvertiblePair> result = new HashSet<>();
            result.add(new ConvertiblePair(Optional.class, String.class));
            result.add(new ConvertiblePair(String.class, Optional.class));
            return result;
        }
    });
    return this;
}

649	### Summary:
The `getPrimitivePromotionCost` method calculates the cost of promoting a primitive type from `srcClass` to `destClass`. It first unwraps the source class if it is a wrapper class, adding a slight penalty. Then, it iterates through an ordered array of primitive types, incrementing the cost by 0.1 for each step until it reaches the destination class or the end of the array. If the destination class is not reached, the cost is adjusted based on the current primitive type.
650	This method calculates the total transformation cost for converting a set of source arguments to a set of destination arguments based on the types of the arguments. It first checks if the number of source arguments is less than the number of destination arguments, in which case it returns `Float.MAX_VALUE`. Then, it iterates through the normal arguments (excluding the varargs) and calculates the transformation cost for each pair of source and destination arguments using the `getObjectTransformationCost` method. If the method is a varargs method, it handles three special cases: when no varargs are passed, when an explicit array is passed for the varargs, and when the varargs are passed as individual arguments. In each case, it calculates the transformation cost for the varargs and adds it to the total cost. Finally, it returns the total transformation cost.
651	```java
/**
 * Calculates the transformation cost from a source class to a destination class.
 * 
 * @param srcClass The source class.
 * @param destClass The destination class.
 * @return The transformation cost as a float.
 */
private static float getObjectTransformationCost(Class<?> srcClass, Class<?> destClass) {
    if (destClass.isPrimitive()) {
        return getPrimitivePromotionCost(srcClass, destClass);
    }
    float cost = 0.0f;
    while (srcClass != null && !destClass.equals(srcClass)) {
        if (destClass.isInterface() && ClassUtils.isAssignable(srcClass, destClass)) {
            cost += 0.25f;
            break;
        }
        cost++;
        srcClass = srcClass.getSuperclass();
    }
    if (srcClass == null) {
        cost += 1.5f;
    }
    return cost;
}
```

public void cast_numeric(Type from, Type to) {
    if (from != to) {
        switch (from) {
            case DOUBLE_TYPE:
                switch (to) {
                    case FLOAT_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.D2F); break;
                    case LONG_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.D2L); break;
                    default: mv.visitInsn(Constants.D2I); cast_numeric(Type.INT_TYPE, to); break;
                }
                break;
            case FLOAT_TYPE:
                switch (to) {
                    case DOUBLE_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.F2D); break;
                    case LONG_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.F2L); break;
                    default: mv.visitInsn(Constants.F2I); cast_numeric(Type.INT_TYPE, to); break;
                }
                break;
            case LONG_TYPE:
                switch (to) {
                    case DOUBLE_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.L2D); break;
                    case FLOAT_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.L2F); break;
                    default: mv.visitInsn(Constants.L2I); cast_numeric(Type.INT_TYPE, to); break;
                }
                break;
            default:
                switch (to) {
                    case BYTE_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.I2B); break;
                    case CHAR_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.I2C); break;
                    case DOUBLE_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.I2D); break;
                    case FLOAT_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.I2F); break;
                    case LONG_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.I2L); break;
                    case SHORT_TYPE: mv.visitInsn(Constants.I2S); break;
                }
                break;
        }
    }
}

public void zero_or_null(Type type) {

        switch (type.getSort()) {
            case Type.DOUBLE: push(0d); break;
            case Type.LONG: push(0L); break;
            case Type.FLOAT: push(0f); break;

            default: push(0);
        }
    } else {
        aconst_null();
    }
}

public void unbox_or_zero(Type type) {
    if (TypeUtils.isPrimitive(type)) {
        if (type != Type.VOID_TYPE) {
            Label nonNull = make_label();
            Label end = make_label();
            dup();
            ifnonnull(nonNull);
            pop();
            zero_or_null(type);
            goTo(end);
            mark(nonNull);
            unbox(type);
            mark(end);
        }
    } else {
        checkcast(type);
    }
}
```

**Summary:**
The method `unbox_or_zero` checks if the given `Type` is a primitive type. If it is, and not `VOID_TYPE`, it duplicates the value, checks if it is non-null, and if so, unboxes it; otherwise, it sets it to zero or null. If the type is not primitive, it simply casts the value to the given type.

public static void process_array(CodeEmitter e, Type type, ProcessArrayCallback callback) {
    Type componentType = TypeUtils.getComponentType(type);
    Local array = e.make_local();
    Local loopvar = e.make_local(Type.INT_TYPE);
    Label loopbody = e.make_label();
    Label checkloop = e.make_label();

    e.store_local(array);
    e.push(0);
    e.store_local(loopvar);
    e.goTo(checkloop);

    e.mark(loopbody);
    e.load_local(array);
    e.load_local(loopvar);
    e.array_load(componentType);
    callback.processElement(componentType);
    e.iinc(loopvar, 1);

    e.mark(checkloop);
    e.load_local(loopvar);
    e.load_local(array);
    e.arraylength();
    e.if_icmp(e.LT, loopbody);
}
```

**Summary:**
The `process_array` method processes elements of an array using a callback. It initializes local variables for the array and loop index, then enters a loop that iterates over each element of the array. During each iteration, it loads the current element, calls the `processElement` method of the provided callback, and increments the loop index. The loop continues until all elements have been processed.
665	```java
/**
 * Compares two objects and jumps to different labels based on their nullity.
 *
 * @param e          the CodeEmitter to generate bytecode
 * @param oneNull    the label to jump to if only one of the objects is null
 * @param bothNull   the label to jump to if both objects are null
 */
private static void nullcmp(CodeEmitter e, Label oneNull, Label bothNull) {
    e.dup2(); // Duplicate the top two elements on the stack
    Label nonNull = e.make_label(); // Label for the case where both objects are non-null
    Label oneNullHelper = e.make_label(); // Helper label for the case where only one object is null
    Label end = e.make_label(); // End label

    e.ifnonnull(nonNull); // If the top element is non-null, jump to nonNull
    e.ifnonnull(oneNullHelper); // If the second top element is non-null, jump to oneNullHelper
    e.pop2(); // Pop the top two elements from the stack
    e.goTo(bothNull); // Jump to bothNull

    e.mark(nonNull); // Mark the nonNull label
    e.ifnull(oneNullHelper); // If the top element is null, jump to oneNullHelper
    e.goTo(end); // Jump to end

    e.mark(oneNullHelper); // Mark the oneNullHelper label
    e.pop2(); // Pop the top two elements from the stack
    e.goTo(oneNull); // Jump to oneNull

    e.mark(end); // Mark the end label
}
```

689	```java
public HttpRequest cookies(final Cookie... cookies) {
    if (cookies.length == 0) {
        return this;
    }
    StringBuilder cookieString = new StringBuilder();
    boolean first = true;
    for (Cookie cookie : cookies) {
        Integer maxAge = cookie.getMaxAge();
        if (maxAge != null && maxAge.intValue() == 0) {
            continue;
        }
        if (!first) {
            cookieString.append("; ");
        }
        first = false;
        cookieString.append(cookie.getName());
        cookieString.append(' ');
        cookieString.append(cookie.getValue());
    }
    headerOverwrite("cookie", cookieString.toString());
    return this;
}
```

**Summary:**

/**
 * Builds an HTTP request buffer.
 *
 * @param fullRequest Indicates if the request is full.
 * @return The constructed HTTP request buffer.
 */
protected Buffer buffer(final boolean fullRequest) {
    // Initialization
    if (header(HEADER_HOST) == null) {
        setHostHeader();
    }
    Buffer formBuffer = formBuffer();
    String queryString = queryString();
    if (header("User-Agent") == null) {
        header("User-Agent", Defaults.userAgent);
    }
    if (method.equals("POST") && contentLength() == null) {
        contentLength(0);
    }

    // Build the request buffer
    Buffer request = new Buffer();
    request.append(method).append(SPACE).append(path);
    if (query != null && !query.isEmpty()) {
        request.append(' ').append(queryString);
    }
    request.append(SPACE).append(httpVersion).append(CRLF);
    populateHeaderAndBody(request, formBuffer, fullRequest);
    return request;
}

699	```java
/**
 * Removes a range of handlers from a linked list of handlers.
 *
 * @param firstHandler The first handler in the linked list.
 * @param start The start label of the range to remove.
 * @param end The end label of the range to remove.
 * @return The updated linked list of handlers with the specified range removed.
 */
static Handler removeRange(final Handler firstHandler, final Label start, final Label end) {
    if (firstHandler == null) {
        return null;
    }

    firstHandler.nextHandler = removeRange(firstHandler.nextHandler, start, end);

    int handlerStart = firstHandler.startPc.bytecodeOffset;
    int handlerEnd = firstHandler.endPc.bytecodeOffset;
    int rangeStart = start.bytecodeOffset;
    int rangeEnd = end == null ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : end.bytecodeOffset;

    if (rangeStart >= handlerEnd || rangeEnd <= handlerStart) {
        return firstHandler;
    }

    if (rangeStart <= handlerStart) {
        if (rangeEnd >= handlerEnd) {
            return firstHandler.nextHandler;
        } else {
            return new Handler(firstHandler, end, firstHandler.endPc);
        }
    } else if (rangeEnd >= handlerEnd) {
        return new Handler(firstHandler, firstHandler.startPc, start);
    } else {
        firstHandler.nextHandler = new Handler(firstHandler, end, firstHandler.endPc);
        return new Handler(firstHandler, firstHandler.startPc, start);
    }
}
```

/**
 * Sets a simple property on a bean.
 * 
 * @param bp The BeanProperty object representing the property to set.
 * @param value The value to set for the property.
 * @throws BeanException If the property is not found and silent mode is not enabled.
 */
protected void setSimpleProperty(final BeanProperty bp, final Object value) {
    Setter setter = bp.getSetter(isDeclared);
    if (setter != null) {
        invokeSetter(setter, bp, value);
        return;
    }
    if (bp.isMap()) {
        ((Map) bp.bean).put(bp.name, value);
        return;
    }
    if (isSilent) {
        return;
    }
    throw new BeanException("Simple property not found: " + bp.name, bp);
}

721	```java
/**
 * Injects uploaded files from a multipart request into the provided targets.
 * 
 * @param servletRequest The HttpServletRequest containing the multipart files.
 * @param targets The Targets object to which the files will be injected.
 */
protected void injectUploadedFiles(final HttpServletRequest servletRequest, final Targets targets) {
    if (!(servletRequest instanceof MultipartRequestWrapper)) {
        return;
    }
    final MultipartRequestWrapper multipartRequest = (MultipartRequestWrapper) servletRequest;
    if (!multipartRequest.isMultipart()) {
        return;
    }
    final Enumeration<String> paramNames = multipartRequest.getFileParameterNames();
    while (paramNames.hasMoreElements()) {
        final String paramName = paramNames.nextElement();
        if (servletRequest.getAttribute(paramName) != null) {
            continue;
        }
        targets.forEachTargetAndIn(this, (target, in) -> {
            final String name = in.matchedName(paramName);
            if (name != null) {
                final FileUpload[] paramValues = multipartRequest.getFiles(paramName);
                if (ignoreInvalidUploadFiles) {
                    for (int j = 0; j < paramValues.length; j++) {
                        final FileUpload paramValue = paramValues[j];
                        if ((!paramValue.isValid()) || (!paramValue.isUploaded())) {
                            paramValues[j] = null;
                        }
                    }
                }
                final Object value = (paramValues.length == 1 ? paramValues[0] : paramValues);
                target.writeValue(name, value, true);
            }
        });
    }
}
```

732	```java
/**
 * Splits a filename into its components: prefix, path, base name, and extension.
 *
 * @param filename The filename to split.
 * @return An array containing the prefix, path, base name, and extension of the filename.
 */
public static String[] split(final String filename) {
    String prefix = getPrefix(filename);
    if (prefix == null) {
        prefix = StringPool.EMPTY;
    }
    int lastSeparatorIndex = indexOfLastSeparator(filename);
    int lastExtensionIndex = indexOfExtension(filename);
    String path;
    String baseName;
    String extension;

    if (lastSeparatorIndex == -1) {
        path = StringPool.EMPTY;
        if (lastExtensionIndex == -1) {
            baseName = filename.substring(prefix.length());
            extension = StringPool.EMPTY;
        } else {
            baseName = filename.substring(prefix.length(), lastExtensionIndex);
            extension = filename.substring(lastExtensionIndex + 1);
        }
    } else {
        path = filename.substring(prefix.length(), lastSeparatorIndex + 1);
        if (lastExtensionIndex == -1) {
            baseName = filename.substring(prefix.length() + path.length());
            extension = StringPool.EMPTY;
        } else {
            baseName = filename.substring(prefix.length() + path.length(), lastExtensionIndex);
            extension = filename.substring(lastExtensionIndex + 1);
        }
    }

    return new String[] { prefix, path, baseName, extension };
}
```

743	```java
/**
 * Scans a JAR file for class and resource entries.
 * 
 * @param file The JAR file to scan.
 */
protected void scanJarFile(final File file) {
    ZipFile zipFile = null;
    try {
        zipFile = new ZipFile(file);
        Enumeration entries = zipFile.entries();
        while (entries.hasMoreElements()) {
            ZipEntry zipEntry = (ZipEntry) entries.nextElement();
            String zipEntryName = zipEntry.getName();
            if (StringUtil.endsWithIgnoreCase(zipEntryName, CLASS_FILE_EXT)) {
                scanEntry(new ClassPathEntry(prepareEntryName(zipEntryName, true), zipFile, zipEntry));
            } else if (includeResources) {
                scanEntry(new ClassPathEntry(prepareEntryName(zipEntryName, false), zipFile, zipEntry));
            }
        }
    } catch (IOException ioex) {
        if (!ignoreException) {
            throw new FindFileException("Invalid zip: " + file.getName(), ioex);
        }
    } catch (RuntimeException rex) {
        if (!ignoreException) {
            ZipUtil.close(zipFile);
            throw rex;
        }
    } finally {
        ZipUtil.close(zipFile);
    }
}
```
744	The `scanClassPath` method is a protected method that scans a classpath for Java class files and resources. It takes a `File` object representing the root directory of the classpath as a parameter. The method first constructs the absolute path of the root directory and appends a file separator if it's not already present. It then creates a `FindFile` object to search for files in the root directory and its subdirectories, excluding directories. The method iterates over each file found by the `FindFile` object, and if the file is a Java class file (based on its extension), it calls the `scanClassFile` method with the file path, root path, file object, and a boolean indicating whether the file is a class file. If the file is a resource and the `includeResources` flag is set to true, it also calls the `scanClassFile` method. If a `RuntimeException` is thrown during the scanning process, the method checks the `ignoreException` flag. If the flag is false, it rethrows the exception; otherwise, it ignores the exception.

/**
 * Retrieves an existing scope of the specified type or initializes a new one if it does not exist.
 *
 * @param madvocScopeType The type of the scope to retrieve or initialize.
 * @return The existing or newly initialized scope.
 * @throws MadvocException if an error occurs while creating the scope.
 */
protected MadvocScope getOrInitScope(final Class<? extends MadvocScope> madvocScopeType) {
    for (final MadvocScope s : allScopes) {
        if (s.getClass().equals(madvocScopeType)) {
            return s;
        }
    }
    // New scope detected
    final MadvocScope newScope;
    try {
        newScope = madpc.createBean(madvocScopeType);
    } catch (Exception ex) {
        throw new MadvocException("Unable to create scope: " + madvocScopeType, ex);
    }
    allScopes.add(newScope);
    return newScope;
}

/**
 * Resolves a scope of a given type.
 * 
 * @param <S> The type of the scope to resolve.
 * @param scopeType The class representing the scope type.
 * @return The resolved scope.
 * @throws PetiteException If an invalid Petite scope is encountered.
 */
@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
public <S extends Scope> S resolveScope(final Class<S> scopeType) {
    S scope = (S) scopes.get(scopeType);
    if (scope == null) {
        try {
            scope = newInternalInstance(scopeType, (PetiteContainer) this);
        } catch (Exception ex) {
            throw new PetiteException("Invalid Petite scope: " + scopeType.getName(), ex);
        }
        registerScope(scopeType, scope);
        scopes.put(scopeType, scope);
    }
    return scope;
}

761	```java
/**
 * Registers a bean with the given type, name, scope, and wiring mode.
 * 
 * @param <T> the type of the bean
 * @param type the class of the bean
 * @param name the name of the bean
 * @param scopeType the scope type of the bean
 * @param wiringMode the wiring mode of the bean
 * @param define whether to define the bean
 * @param consumer a consumer to configure the bean
 * @return the bean definition
 * @throws PetiteException if a bean with the same name already exists or if the type is an interface
 */
public <T> BeanDefinition<T> registerPetiteBean(final Class<T> type, String name, Class<? extends Scope> scopeType, WiringMode wiringMode, final boolean define, final Consumer<T> consumer) {
    // Resolve bean name and wiring mode if not provided
    if (name == null) name = resolveBeanName(type);
    if (wiringMode == null) wiringMode = annotationResolver.resolveBeanWiringMode(type);
    if (wiringMode == WiringMode.DEFAULT) wiringMode = petiteConfig.getDefaultWiringMode();
    if (scopeType == null) scopeType = annotationResolver.resolveBeanScopeType(type);
    if (scopeType == null) scopeType = SingletonScope.class;

    // Remove existing bean with the same name
    BeanDefinition existing = removeBean(name);
    if (existing != null) {
        if (petiteConfig.getDetectDuplicatedBeanNames()) {
            throw new PetiteException("Duplicated bean name detected while registering class '" + type.getName() + "'. Petite bean class '" + existing.type.getName() + "' is already registered with the name: " + name);
        }
    }

    // Check if the type is valid
    if (type.isInterface()) {
        throw new PetiteException("PetiteBean can not be an interface: " + type.getName());
    }

    // Log the registration
    if (log.isDebugEnabled()) {
        log.info("Petite bean: [" + name + "] --> " + type.getName() + " @ " + scopeType.getSimpleName() + ":" + wiringMode.toString());
    }

    // Resolve scope and create bean definition
    Scope scope = resolveScope(scopeType);
    BeanDefinition<T> beanDefinition = createBeanDefinitionForRegistration(name, type, scope, wiringMode, consumer);
    registerBean(name, beanDefinition);

    // Resolve provider definitions and register them

764	```java
/**
 * Resolves bean names for a given type.
 * 
 * @param type The class type to resolve bean names for.
 * @return An array of bean names that match the given type.
 */
protected String[] resolveBeanNamesForType(final Class type) {
    // Retrieve bean names from cache
    String[] beanNames = beanCollections.get(type);
    if (beanNames != null) {
        return beanNames;
    }

    // Create a list to store matching bean names
    ArrayList<String> list = new ArrayList<>();

    // Iterate through all bean definitions
    for (Map.Entry<String, BeanDefinition> entry : beans.entrySet()) {
        BeanDefinition beanDefinition = entry.getValue();
        // Check if the bean definition type matches the given type
        if (ClassUtil.isTypeOf(beanDefinition.type, type)) {
            String beanName = entry.getKey();
            list.add(beanName);
        }
    }

    // If no matching bean names are found, return an empty array
    if (list.isEmpty()) {
        beanNames = StringPool.EMPTY_ARRAY;
    } else {
        // Convert the list to an array and store in cache
        beanNames = list.toArray(new String[0]);
    }

    // Store the resolved bean names in cache
    beanCollections.put(type, beanNames);
    return beanNames;
}

765	```java
/**
 * Registers a constructor injection point for a bean.
 *
 * @param beanName   the name of the bean
 * @param paramTypes the parameter types of the constructor
 * @param references the references to be injected
 * @throws PetiteException if no suitable constructor is found or multiple constructors are found
 */
public void registerPetiteCtorInjectionPoint(final String beanName, final Class<?>[] paramTypes, final String[] references) {
    BeanDefinition beanDefinition = lookupExistingBeanDefinition(beanName);
    ClassDescriptor cd = ClassIntrospector.get().lookup(beanDefinition.type);
    Constructor<?> constructor = null;

    if (paramTypes == null) {
        CtorDescriptor[] ctors = cd.getAllCtorDescriptors();
        if (ctors != null && ctors.length > 0) {
            if (ctors.length > 1) {
                throw new PetiteException(ctors.length + " suitable constructor found as injection point for: " + beanDefinition.type.getName());
            }
            constructor = ctors[0].getConstructor();
        }
    } else {
        CtorDescriptor ctorDescriptor = cd.getCtorDescriptor(paramTypes, true);
        if (ctorDescriptor != null) {
            constructor = ctorDescriptor.getConstructor();
        }
    }

    if (constructor == null) {
        throw new PetiteException("Constructor not found: " + beanDefinition.type.getName());
    }

    BeanReferences[] ref = referencesResolver.resolveReferenceFromValues(constructor, references);
    beanDefinition.ctor = new CtorInjectionPoint(constructor, ref);
}
```

/**
 * Registers a method injection point for a given bean.
 * 
 * @param beanName The name of the bean.
 * @param methodName The name of the method.
 * @param arguments The arguments of the method.
 * @param references The references to be resolved.
 * 
 * @throws PetiteException If the method is not found or if multiple suitable methods are found.
 */
public void registerPetiteMethodInjectionPoint(final String beanName, final String methodName, final Class<?>[] arguments, final String[] references) {
    BeanDefinition beanDefinition = lookupExistingBeanDefinition(beanName);
    ClassDescriptor cd = ClassIntrospector.get().lookup(beanDefinition.type);
    Method method = null;

    if (arguments == null) {
        MethodDescriptor[] methods = cd.getAllMethodDescriptors(methodName);
        if (methods != null && methods.length > 0) {
            if (methods.length > 1) {
                throw new PetiteException(methods.length + " suitable methods found as injection points for: " + beanDefinition.type.getName() + ' ' + methodName);
            }
            method = methods[0].getMethod();
        }
    } else {
        MethodDescriptor md = cd.getMethodDescriptor(methodName, arguments, true);
        if (md != null) {
            method = md.getMethod();
        }
    }

    if (method == null) {
        throw new PetiteException("Method not found: " + beanDefinition.type.getName() + ' ' + methodName);
    }

    BeanReferences[] ref = referencesResolver.resolveReferenceFromValues(method, references);
    MethodInjectionPoint mip = new MethodInjectionPoint(method, ref);
    beanDefinition.addMethodInjectionPoint(mip);
}
```

public void registerPetiteInitMethods(final String beanName, final InitMethodInvocationStrategy invocationStrategy, String... initMethodNames) {

}

775	```java
@Override
public Object intercept(final ActionRequest actionRequest) throws Exception {
    printBefore(actionRequest);
    long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
    Object result = null;
    try {
        result = actionRequest.invoke();
    } catch (Exception ex) {
        result = "<exception>";
        throw ex;
    } catch (Throwable th) {
        result = "<throwable>";
        throw new Exception(th);
    } finally {
        long executionTime = System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime;
        printAfter(actionRequest, executionTime, result);
    }
    return result;
}
```

**Summary:**
The `intercept` method is an overridden method that takes an `ActionRequest` object as a parameter and returns an `Object`. It performs the following steps:
1. Calls `printBefore` to log or perform some action before the request is processed.
2. Records the start time.
3. Attempts to invoke the `actionRequest` and captures the result.
4. If an `Exception` is caught, it sets the result to `"<exception>"` and rethrows the exception.
5. If a `Throwable` is caught, it sets the result to `"<throwable>"` and rethrows a new `Exception` wrapping the `Throwable`.
6. Regardless of the outcome, it calculates the execution time by subtracting the start time from the current time.
7. Calls `printAfter` to log or perform some action after the request is processed, passing the execution time and result.
8. Returns the result.

public static void pushInt(final MethodVisitor mv, final int value) {
    if (value <= 5) {
        mv.visitInsn(ICONST_0 + value);
    } else if (value <= Byte.MAX_VALUE) {
        mv.visitIntInsn(BIPUSH, value);
    } else {
        mv.visitIntInsn(SIPUSH, value);
    }
}
```

**Summary:**
The `pushInt` method is used to push an integer value onto the operand stack of a method being visited by a `MethodVisitor`. It selects the appropriate opcode based on the value:
- If the value is between 0 and 5, it uses `ICONST_0` to `ICONST_5` opcodes.
- If the value is between 6 and 127, it uses the `BIPUSH` opcode.
- If the value is between 128 and 32767, it uses the `SIPUSH` opcode.

784	```java
public static void loadMethodArgument(MethodVisitor mv, MethodInfo methodInfo, int index) {
    int offset = methodInfo.getArgumentOffset(index);
    int type = methodInfo.getArgument(index).getOpcode();
    switch (type) {
        case 'I': mv.visitVarInsn(ILOAD, offset); break;
        case 'J': mv.visitVarInsn(LLOAD, offset); break;
        case 'F': mv.visitVarInsn(FLOAD, offset); break;
        case 'D': mv.visitVarInsn(DLOAD, offset); break;
        default: mv.visitVarInsn(ALOAD, offset);
    }
}
```

        case 'F': mv.visitVarInsn(FSTORE, offset); break;
        case 'D': mv.visitVarInsn(DSTORE, offset); break;

public static void prepareReturnValue(MethodVisitor mv, MethodInfo methodInfo, int varOffset) {
    varOffset += methodInfo.getAllArgumentsSize();
    switch (methodInfo.getReturnType().getOpcode()) {
        case 'V': mv.visitInsn(ACONST_NULL); break;
        case 'B': AsmUtil.valueOfByte(mv); break;
        case 'C': AsmUtil.valueOfCharacter(mv); break;
        case 'S': AsmUtil.valueOfShort(mv); break;
        case 'I': AsmUtil.valueOfInteger(mv); break;
        case 'Z': AsmUtil.valueOfBoolean(mv); break;
        case 'J': AsmUtil.valueOfLong(mv); break;
        case 'F': AsmUtil.valueOfFloat(mv); break;
        case 'D': AsmUtil.valueOfDouble(mv); break;
    }
}

/**
 * Creates a method signature key based on the provided access level, method name, description, and class name.
 * 
 * @param access The access level of the method.
 * @param methodName The name of the method.
 * @param description A description of the method.
 * @param className The name of the class containing the method.
 * @return A string representing the method signature key.
 */
public static String createMethodSignaturesKey(final int access, final String methodName, final String description, final String className) {
    return new StringBand(7)
        .append(access)
        .append(COLON)
        .append(description)
        .append(StringPool.UNDERSCORE)
        .append(className)
        .append(StringPool.HASH)
        .append(methodName)
        .toString();
}

public static void newArray(MethodVisitor mv, Class componentType) {

    }

        return;

/**
 * Checks if the given Flags object is empty.
 * 
 * @param flags The Flags object to check.
 * @return true if the Flags object is empty (i.e., both systemFlags and userFlags are null or empty), false otherwise.
 */
public static boolean isEmptyFlags(Flags flags) {
    if (flags == null) return true;
    Flags.Flag[] systemFlags = flags.getSystemFlags();
    if (systemFlags != null && systemFlags.length > 0) return false;
    String[] userFlags = flags.getUserFlags();
    if (userFlags != null && userFlags.length > 0) return false;
    return true;
}

/**
 * Extracts the Bearer token from the Authorization header of an HTTP request.
 *
 * @param request The HTTP request containing the Authorization header.
 * @return The Bearer token if found, otherwise null.
 */
public static String resolveAuthBearerToken(final HttpServletRequest request) {
    String header = request.getHeader(HEADER_AUTHORIZATION);
    if (header == null) {
        return null;
    }
    int ndx = header.indexOf("Bearer ");
    if (ndx == -1) {
        return null;
    }
    return header.substring(ndx + 7).trim();
}

795	```java
public static void prepareResponse(final HttpServletResponse response, final String fileName, String mimeType, final int fileSize) {
    // Set the content type based on the file extension if mimeType is null
    if (mimeType == null && fileName != null) {
        String extension = FileNameUtil.getExtension(fileName);
        mimeType = MimeTypes.getMimeType(extension);
    }
    // Set the content type if it is not null
    if (mimeType != null) {
        response.setContentType(mimeType);
    }
    // Set the content length if it is non-negative
    if (fileSize >= 0) {
        response.setContentLength(fileSize);
    }
    // Support internationalization by setting the content disposition header
    if (fileName != null) {
        String name = FileNameUtil.getName(fileName);
        String encodedFileName = URLCoder.encode(name);
        response.setHeader(CONTENT_DISPOSITION, "attachment;filename=\"" + name + "\";filename*=utf8''" + encodedFileName);
    }
}

1. **Validation of Salt**: The method first checks if the salt is in the correct format. It ensures that the salt starts with two spaces, followed by an optional minor version character and two digits representing the number of rounds. If the salt format is invalid, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`.

2. **Extraction of Rounds**: The method extracts the number of rounds from the salt. If the number of rounds is missing or exceeds the maximum allowed (30), it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`.

4. **Decoding Salt**: The method decodes the salt from a base64-encoded string to a byte array.

5. **Hashing**: The method uses the bcrypt library to hash the password. It creates a new `BCrypt` object and calls the `crypt_raw` method to perform the hashing.

6. **Formatting Output**: The method formats the hashed password into a string that includes the bcrypt identifier, minor version (if present), number of rounds, and the salt and hashed values encoded in base64.

7. **Return Value**: The method returns the formatted hashed password as a string.

In summary, the `hashpw` method securely hashes a password using the bcrypt algorithm with a given salt, ensuring the output is in a standardized format.

/**
 * Reads the package action path for a given action class.
 * 
 * @param actionClass The class for which to read the package action path.
 * @return An array containing the package action path, or null if not found.
 */
protected String[] readPackageActionPath(final Class actionClass) {
    Package actionPackage = actionClass.getPackage();
    String actionPackageName = actionPackage.getName();

    // 1 - read annotations first
    String packageActionPathFromAnnotation = null;
    while (true) {
        MadvocAction madvocActionAnnotation = actionPackage.getAnnotation(MadvocAction.class);
        packageActionPathFromAnnotation = madvocActionAnnotation != null ? madvocActionAnnotation.value().trim() : null;
        if (StringUtil.isEmpty(packageActionPathFromAnnotation)) {
            packageActionPathFromAnnotation = null;
        }
        if (packageActionPathFromAnnotation == null) {
            // next package
            String newPackage = actionPackage.getName();
            actionPackage = null;
            while (actionPackage == null) {
                final int ndx = newPackage.lastIndexOf(' ');
                if (ndx == -1) {
                    // end of hierarchy, nothing found
                    break;
                }
                newPackage = newPackage.substring(0, ndx);
                actionPackage = Packages.of(actionClass.getClassLoader(), newPackage);
            }
        } else {
            // annotation found, register root
            rootPackages.addRootPackage(actionPackage.getName(), packageActionPathFromAnnotation);
            break;
        }
    }

    // 2 - read root package
    String packagePath = rootPackages.findPackagePathForActionPackage(actionPackageName);
    if (packagePath == null) {
        return ArraysUtil.array(null, null);
    }
    return ArraysUtil.array(StringUtil.stripChar(packagePath, ' '), StringUtil.surround(packagePath, StringPool.SLASH));
}
```
830	```java
/**
 * Reads the action path for a given method.
 *
 * @param methodName The name of the method.
 * @param annotationValues The annotation values.
 * @param actionConfig The action configuration.
 * @return An array containing the method name and the action path.
 */
protected String[] readMethodActionPath(final String methodName, final ActionAnnotationValues annotationValues, final ActionConfig actionConfig) {
    // Retrieve the method action path from the annotation values, or use the method name if not provided
    String methodActionPath = annotationValues != null ? annotationValues.value() : methodName;
    if (methodActionPath == null) {
        methodActionPath = methodName;
    } else if (methodActionPath.equals(Action.NONE)) {
        return ArraysUtil.array(null, null);
    }

    // Check for default action paths in the action configuration
    for (String path : actionConfig.getActionMethodNames()) {
        if (methodActionPath.equals(path)) {
            methodActionPath = null;
            break;
        }
    }

    // Return an array containing the method name and the action path
    return ArraysUtil.array(methodName, methodActionPath);
}
```

832	```java
public ActionRuntime createActionRuntime(
    ActionHandler actionHandler,
    Class actionClass,
    Method actionClassMethod,
    Class<? extends ActionResult> actionResult,
    Class<? extends ActionResult> defaultActionResult,
    ActionFilter[] filters,
    ActionInterceptor[] interceptors,
    ActionDefinition actionDefinition,
    boolean async,
    boolean auth
) {
    if (actionHandler != null) {
        return new ActionRuntime(
            actionHandler,
            actionClass,
            actionClassMethod,
            filters,
            interceptors,
            actionDefinition,
            NoneActionResult.class,
            NoneActionResult.class,
            async,
            auth,
            null,
            null
        );
    }

    ScopeData scopeData = scopeDataInspector.inspectClassScopes(actionClass);
    Class<?>[] paramTypes = actionClassMethod.getParameterTypes();
    MethodParam[] params = new MethodParam[paramTypes.length];
    Annotation[][] paramAnns = actionClassMethod.getParameterAnnotations();
    String[] methodParamNames = null;

    for (int ndx = 0; ndx < paramTypes.length; ndx++) {
        Class<?> paramType = paramTypes[ndx];
        if (methodParamNames == null) {
            methodParamNames = actionMethodParamNameResolver.resolveParamNames(actionClassMethod);
        }
        String paramName = methodParamNames[ndx];
        Annotation[] parameterAnnotations = paramAnns[ndx];
        ScopeData paramsScopeData = scopeDataInspector.inspectMethodParameterScopes(paramName, paramType, parameterAnnotations);
        MapperFunction mapperFunction = null;

        for (final Annotation annotation : parameterAnnotations) {
            if (annotation instanceof Mapper) {
                mapperFunction = MapperFunctionInstances.get().lookup(((Mapper) annotation).value());
                break;
            }
        }

        params[ndx] = new MethodParam(
            paramTypes[ndx],
            paramName,
            scopeDataInspector.detectAnnotationType(parameterAnnotations),
            paramsScopeData,
            mapperFunction
        );
    }

    return new ActionRuntime(
        null,
        actionClass,
        actionClassMethod,
        filters,
        interceptors,
        actionDefinition,
        actionResult,
        defaultActionResult,
        async,
        auth,
        scopeData,
        params
    );
}
```

/**
 * Applies advice to a target class.
 * 
 * @param <T> the type of the target class
 * @param targetClass the target class to apply advice to
 * @return an instance of the advice class with the target class injected
 * @throws ProxettaException if an error occurs during advice application
 */
public static <T> T applyAdvice(final Class<T> targetClass) {
    Class adviceClass = cache.get(targetClass);
    if (adviceClass == null) {
        // Create new advice class if not already created
        adviceClass = PROXY_PROXETTA.proxy().setTarget(targetClass).define();
        cache.put(targetClass, adviceClass);
    }
    // Create new advice instance and inject target instance
    try {
        Object advice = ClassUtil.newInstance(adviceClass);
        Field field = adviceClass.getField("$___target$0");
        field.set(advice, targetClass);
        return (T) advice;
    } catch (Exception ex) {
        throw new ProxettaException(ex);
    }
}

/**
 * Finds the subclass type data for a given class.
 *
 * @param type The class to find the subclass type data for.
 * @return The subclass type data if found, or null otherwise.
 */
protected TypeData findSubclassTypeData(final Class type) {
    final Class<? extends Annotation> defaultAnnotation = jsonAnnotation;
    if (type.getAnnotation(defaultAnnotation) != null) {
        // Current type has annotation, don't find anything, let type data be created
        return null;
    }
    ClassDescriptor cd = ClassIntrospector.get().lookup(type);
    // Lookup superclasses
    Class<?>[] superClasses = cd.getAllSuperclasses();
    for (Class<?> superClass : superClasses) {
        if (superClass.getAnnotation(defaultAnnotation) != null) {
            // Annotated subclass found!
            return _lookupTypeData(superClass);
        }
    }
    // Lookup interfaces
    Class<?>[] interfaces = cd.getAllInterfaces();
    for (Class<?> interfaze : interfaces) {
        if (interfaze.getAnnotation(defaultAnnotation) != null) {
            // Annotated subclass found!
            return _lookupTypeData(interfaze);
        }
    }
    return null;
}
```

845	```java
/**
 * Copies the bootstrap methods from a ClassReader to a char buffer.
 * 
 * @param classReader The ClassReader containing the class file.
 * @param charBuffer The char buffer to store the bootstrap methods.
 */
private void copyBootstrapMethods(final ClassReader classReader, final char[] charBuffer) {
    byte[] inputBytes = classReader.b;
    int currentAttributeOffset = classReader.getFirstAttributeOffset();
    
    // Find the 'bootstrap_methods' attribute.
    for (int i = classReader.readUnsignedShort(currentAttributeOffset - 2); i > 0; --i) {
        String attributeName = classReader.readUTF8(currentAttributeOffset, charBuffer);
        if (Constants.BOOTSTRAP_METHODS.equals(attributeName)) {
            bootstrapMethodCount = classReader.readUnsignedShort(currentAttributeOffset + 6);
            break;
        }
        currentAttributeOffset += 6 + classReader.readInt(currentAttributeOffset + 2);
    }
    
    if (bootstrapMethodCount > 0) {
        // Compute the offset and length of the 'bootstrap_methods' array.
        int bootstrapMethodsOffset = currentAttributeOffset + 8;
        int bootstrapMethodsLength = classReader.readInt(currentAttributeOffset + 2) - 2;
        bootstrapMethods = new ByteVector(bootstrapMethodsLength);
        bootstrapMethods.putByteArray(inputBytes, bootstrapMethodsOffset, bootstrapMethodsLength);
        
        // Add each bootstrap method to the symbol table entries.
        int currentOffset = bootstrapMethodsOffset;
        for (int i = 0; i < bootstrapMethodCount; i++) {
            int offset = currentOffset - bootstrapMethodsOffset;
            int bootstrapMethodRef = classReader.readUnsignedShort(currentOffset);
            currentOffset += 2;
            int numBootstrapArguments = classReader.readUnsignedShort(currentOffset);
            currentOffset += 2;
            int hashCode = classReader.readConst(bootstrapMethodRef, charBuffer).hashCode();
            
            while (numBootstrapArguments-- > 0) {
                int bootstrapArgument = classReader.readUnsignedShort(currentOffset);
                currentOffset += 2;
                hashCode ^= classReader.readConst(bootstrapArgument, charBuffer).hashCode();
            }
            
            add(new Entry(i, Symbol.BOOTSTRAP_METHOD_TAG, offset, hashCode & 0x7FFFFFFF));
        }
    }
}
```

private Symbol addConstantIntegerOrFloat(final int tag, final int value) {
    int hashCode = hash(tag, value);
    Entry entry = get(hashCode);
    while (entry != null) {
        if (entry.tag == tag && entry.hashCode == hashCode && entry.data == value) {
            return entry;

        entry = entry.next;
    }
    constantPool.putByte(tag).putInt(value);
    return put(new Entry(constantPoolCount++, tag, value, hashCode));
}

871	```java
/**
 * Computes a hash code for a given string.
 * 
 * @param name The string to hash.
 * @return The computed hash code.
 */
private int hash(final String name) {
    int h = 0;
    for (int i = name.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        char c = name.charAt(i);
        if (!caseSensitive) {
            if (c >= ' ' && c <= ' ') {
                c += 32;
            }
        }
        h = 31 * h + c;
    }
    if (h > 0) {
        return h;
    }
    if (h == Integer.MIN_VALUE) {
        return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
    }
    return -h;
}
```

@Override
public Iterator<Map.Entry<String, V>> iterator() {
    final MapEntry[] e = { head.after };
    return new Iterator<Map.Entry<String, V>>() {
        @Override
        public boolean hasNext() {
            return e[0] != head;
        }

        @Override
        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
        public Map.Entry<String, V> next() {
            if (!hasNext()) {
                throw new NoSuchElementException("No next() entry in the iteration");
            }
            MapEntry<V> next = e[0];
            e[0] = e[0].after;
            return next;
        }

        @Override
        public void remove() {
            throw new UnsupportedOperationException();
        }
    };
}
```

**Summary:**
This method returns an iterator for the map entries. The iterator starts from the first entry after the head and iterates through the map entries until it reaches the head again. The `hasNext` method checks if there are more entries to iterate over, the `next` method returns the next entry and advances the iterator, and the `remove` method is not supported and throws an `UnsupportedOperationException`.

876	The `grow` method is designed to increase the capacity of a buffer array to ensure it can accommodate at least a specified minimum capacity. Here's a summary of the method:

1. **Determine the old capacity**: The current size of the buffer array is stored in `oldCapacity`.
2. **Calculate the new capacity**: The new capacity is calculated by doubling the old capacity (`oldCapacity << 1`). This is a common technique to efficiently increase the size of the buffer.
3. **Check if the new capacity is sufficient**: If the new capacity minus the minimum capacity is less than 0, it means the minimum capacity is larger than the doubled capacity. In this case, the new capacity is set to the minimum capacity plus 512 to ensure it meets the minimum requirement.
4. **Resize the buffer**: The buffer array is resized to the new capacity using `Arrays.copyOf`, which creates a new array with the specified size and copies the elements from the old array to the new array.

This method ensures that the buffer array is always large enough to hold the required data, with an efficient growth strategy that minimizes the number of resizing operations.

881	```java
protected void createFirstChainDelegate_Continue(final TargetMethodData tmd) {
    methodVisitor.visitCode();
    if (tmd.msign.isStatic) {
        loadStaticMethodArguments(methodVisitor, tmd.msign);
        methodVisitor.visitMethodInsn(INVOKESTATIC, wd.thisReference, tmd.firstMethodName(), tmd.msign.getDescription(), false);
    } else {
        loadSpecialMethodArguments(methodVisitor, tmd.msign);
        methodVisitor.visitMethodInsn(INVOKESPECIAL, wd.thisReference, tmd.firstMethodName(), tmd.msign.getDescription(), false);
    }
    visitReturn(methodVisitor, tmd.msign, false);
    methodVisitor.visitMaxs(0, 0);
    methodVisitor.visitEnd();
}
```

**Summary:**
This method, `createFirstChainDelegate_Continue`, is designed to handle the creation of a method chain delegate. It starts by visiting the code of the method using `methodVisitor.visitCode()`. Depending on whether the method is static (`tmd.msign.isStatic`), it either loads static method arguments using `loadStaticMethodArguments` or special method arguments using `loadSpecialMethodArguments`. It then invokes the first method in the chain using `methodVisitor.visitMethodInsn` with the appropriate opcode (`INVOKESTATIC` or `INVOKESPECIAL`). After the method invocation, it returns using `visitReturn` and sets the maximum stack and local variable sizes using `methodVisitor.visitMaxs(0, 0)`. Finally, it ends the method using `methodVisitor.visitEnd()`.

893	The `writeTo` method writes the contents of a list of objects to an output stream. It iterates through each object in the list and checks its type. If the object is an instance of `FastByteBuffer`, it converts the buffer to an array and writes it to the output stream. If the object is an instance of `Uploadable`, it opens an input stream from the object, copies the contents to the output stream using `StreamUtil.copy`, and then closes the input stream.
894	```java
public void writeTo(final OutputStream out, final HttpProgressListener progressListener) throws IOException {
    final int size = size();
    final int callbackSize = progressListener.callbackSize(size);
    int count = 0;
    int step = 0;

    progressListener.transferred(count);

    for (Object o : list) {
        if (o instanceof FastByteBuffer) {
            FastByteBuffer fastByteBuffer = (FastByteBuffer) o;
            byte[] bytes = fastByteBuffer.toArray();
            int offset = 0;

            while (offset < bytes.length) {
                int chunk = callbackSize - step;
                if (offset + chunk > bytes.length) {
                    chunk = bytes.length - offset;
                }
                out.write(bytes, offset, chunk);
                offset += chunk;
                step += chunk;
                count += chunk;

                if (step >= callbackSize) {
                    progressListener.transferred(count);
                    step -= callbackSize;
                }
            }
        } else if (o instanceof Uploadable) {
            Uploadable uploadable = (Uploadable) o;
            InputStream inputStream = uploadable.openInputStream();
            int remaining = uploadable.getSize();

            try {
                while (remaining > 0) {
                    int chunk = callbackSize - step;
                    if (chunk > remaining) {
                        chunk = remaining;
                    }
                    StreamUtil.copy(inputStream, out, chunk);
                    remaining -= chunk;
                    step += chunk;
                    count += chunk;

                    if (step >= callbackSize) {
                        progressListener.transferred(count);
                        step -= callbackSize;
                    }
                }
            } finally {
                StreamUtil.close(inputStream);
            }
        }
    }

    if (step != 0) {
        progressListener.transferred(count);
    }
}
```

915	```java
protected void process() {
    // Check if targetInputStream is null and throw an exception if it is
    if (targetInputStream == null) {
        throw new ProxettaException("Target missing: " + targetClassName);
    }

    // Create a ClassReader to read the class input stream
    ClassReader classReader;
    try {
        classReader = new ClassReader(targetInputStream);
    } catch (IOException ioex) {
        throw new ProxettaException("Error reading class input stream", ioex);
    }

    // Read information using TargetClassInfoReader
    TargetClassInfoReader targetClassInfoReader = new TargetClassInfoReader(proxetta.getClassLoader());
    classReader.accept(targetClassInfoReader, 0);

    // Create a ClassWriter to compute maxs and frames
    this.destClassWriter = new ClassWriter(ClassWriter.COMPUTE_MAXS | ClassWriter.COMPUTE_FRAMES);

    // Log debug information if logging is enabled
    if (log.isDebugEnabled()) {
        log.debug("processing: " + classReader.getClassName());
    }

    // Process the class and store important data
    WorkData wd = process(classReader, targetClassInfoReader);
    proxyApplied = wd.proxyApplied;
    proxyClassName = wd.thisReference.replace(' ', ' ');
}

917	```java
public Class define() {
    process();
    if (!proxetta.isForced() && !isProxyApplied()) {
        if (log.isDebugEnabled()) {
            log.debug("Proxy not applied: " + StringUtil.toSafeString(targetClassName));
        }
        if (targetClass != null) {
            return targetClass;
        }
        if (targetClassName != null) {
            try {
                return ClassLoaderUtil.loadClass(targetClassName);
            } catch (ClassNotFoundException cnfex) {
                throw new ProxettaException(cnfex);
            }
        }
    }
    if (log.isDebugEnabled()) {
        log.debug("Proxy created: " + StringUtil.toSafeString(targetClassName));
    }
    try {
        ClassLoader classLoader = proxetta.getClassLoader();
        if (classLoader == null) {
            classLoader = ClassLoaderUtil.getDefaultClassLoader();
            if ((classLoader == null) && (targetClass != null)) {
                classLoader = targetClass.getClassLoader();
            }
        }
        final byte[] bytes = toByteArray();
        dumpClassInDebugFolder(bytes);
        return DefineClass.of(getProxyClassName(), bytes, classLoader);
    } catch (Exception ex) {
        throw new ProxettaException("Class definition failed", ex);
    }
}

protected void dumpClassInDebugFolder(final byte[] bytes) {

        return;
    }

        fileName = "proxetta-" + System.currentTimeMillis();

935	```java
/**
 * Resolves aliases in a given string.
 * 
 * @param value The input string containing potential aliases.
 * @return The resolved string with aliases replaced by their corresponding values.
 */
protected String resolveAlias(final String value) {
    StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder(value.length());
    int i = 0;
    int len = value.length();
    
    while (i < len) {
        int ndx = value.indexOf(' ', i);
        if (ndx == -1) {
            if (i == 0) {
                String alias = lookupAlias(value);
                return (alias != null) ? alias : value;
            } else {
                result.append(value.substring(i));
            }
            break;
        }
        
        result.append(value.substring(i, ndx));
        ndx++;
        int ndx2 = value.indexOf(' ', ndx);
        String aliasName = (ndx2 == -1) ? value.substring(ndx) : value.substring(ndx, ndx2);
        
        String alias = lookupAlias(aliasName);
        if (alias != null) {
            result.append(alias);
        } else {
            if (log.isWarnEnabled()) {
                log.warn("Alias not found: " + aliasName);
            }
        }
        
        i = ndx2 + 1;
    }
    
    i = 0;
    len = result.length();
    while (i < len) {
        if (result.charAt(i) != ' ') {
            break;
        }
        i++;
    }
    
    if (i > 1) {
        return result.substring(i - 1, len);
    }
    
    return result.toString();
}
```

/**
 * Finds the last occurrence of a dot ('.') in a string, considering spaces as delimiters.
 * If no dot is found, returns the index of the last space. If neither is found, returns -1.
 *
 * @param str The input string to search.
 * @return The index of the last dot or space, or -1 if neither is found.
 */
public static int lastIndexOfSlashDot(final String str) {
    int slashNdx = str.lastIndexOf(' ');
    int dotNdx = StringUtil.lastIndexOf(str, ' ', str.length(), slashNdx);
    if (dotNdx == -1) {
        if (slashNdx == -1) {
            return -1;
        }
        slashNdx++;
        if (slashNdx < str.length() - 1) {
            dotNdx = slashNdx;
        } else {
            dotNdx = -1;
        }
    }
    return dotNdx;
}
```

The `mix` method takes two final integers `j` and `d` as parameters. It performs the following operations:
1. Sets `y[0]` to the sum of `x[0]` and `x[1]`.
2. Calculates a left rotation of `x[1]` by `rotl` bits, where `rotl` is determined by `r[d % DEPTH_OF_D_IN_R][j]`. The result is stored in `y[1]`.

Then, it calculates a right rotation value `rotr` using the modulo operation on `d` with `DEPTH_OF_D_IN_R` and the array `r`. The method then performs a right rotation on `y[1]` by `rotr` bits and stores the result in `x[1]`. Finally, it calculates `x[0]` as the difference between `y[0]` and `x[1]`.

private static String removeAnyBounding(final char s, final char e, final String str) {

        return str;
    }
    if (str.startsWith(String.valueOf(s)) && str.endsWith(String.valueOf(e))) {

958	```java
/**
 * Adds a file or directory to a ZIP output stream.
 *
 * @param zos        the ZIP output stream
 * @param file       the file or directory to add
 * @param path       the path of the file or directory in the ZIP archive
 * @param comment    the comment for the ZIP entry
 * @param recursive  whether to add the directory recursively
 * @throws IOException if an I/O error occurs
 */
public static void addToZip(final ZipOutputStream zos, final File file, String path, final String comment, final boolean recursive) throws IOException {
    if (!file.exists()) {
        throw new FileNotFoundException(file.toString());
    }
    if (path == null) {
        path = file.getName();
    }
    while (path.length() != 0 && path.charAt(0) == ' ') {
        path = path.substring(1);
    }
    boolean isDir = file.isDirectory();
    if (isDir) {
        if (!StringUtil.endsWithChar(path, ' ')) {
            path += ' ';
        }
    }
    ZipEntry zipEntry = new ZipEntry(path);
    zipEntry.setTime(file.lastModified());
    if (comment != null) {
        zipEntry.setComment(comment);
    }
    if (isDir) {
        zipEntry.setSize(0);
        zipEntry.setCrc(0);
    }
    zos.putNextEntry(zipEntry);
    if (!isDir) {
        InputStream is = new FileInputStream(file);
        try {
            StreamUtil.copy(is, zos);
        } finally {
            StreamUtil.close(is);
        }
    }
    zos.closeEntry();
    if (recursive && file.isDirectory()) {
        boolean noRelativePath = StringUtil.isEmpty(path);
        final File[] children = file.listFiles();
        if (children != null && children.length != 0) {
            for (File child : children) {
                String childRelativePath = (noRelativePath ? StringPool.EMPTY : path) + child.getName();
                addToZip(zos, child, childRelativePath, comment, recursive);
            }
        }
    }
}
```
959	```java
public static void addToZip(ZipOutputStream zos, byte[] content, String path, String comment) throws IOException {
    // Trim leading spaces from the path
    while (path.length() != 0 && path.charAt(0) == ' ') {
        path = path.substring(1);
    }
    // Trim trailing spaces from the path
    if (StringUtil.endsWithChar(path, ' ')) {
        path = path.substring(0, path.length() - 1);
    }
    // Create a new ZipEntry with the trimmed path
    ZipEntry zipEntry = new ZipEntry(path);
    // Set the current time as the entry's modification time
    zipEntry.setTime(System.currentTimeMillis());
    // Set the comment for the zip entry if provided
    if (comment != null) {
        zipEntry.setComment(comment);
    }
    // Add the zip entry to the zip output stream
    zos.putNextEntry(zipEntry);
    // Create an input stream from the content bytes
    InputStream is = new ByteArrayInputStream(content);
    try {
        // Copy the content to the zip output stream
        StreamUtil.copy(is, zos);
    } finally {
        // Close the input stream
        StreamUtil.close(is);
    }
    // Close the current zip entry
    zos.closeEntry();
}
```

/**
 * Reads verification type information from a given offset in a bytecode frame.
 *
 * @param verificationTypeInfoOffset The offset in the bytecode where the verification type information starts.
 * @param frame The array representing the current frame.
 * @param index The index in the frame array where the verification type information should be stored.
 * @param charBuffer A buffer to read class names.
 * @param labels An array of labels for uninitialized types.
 * @return The updated offset after reading the verification type information.
 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the tag is not recognized.
 */
private int readVerificationTypeInfo(final int verificationTypeInfoOffset, final Object[] frame, final int index, final char[] charBuffer, final Label[] labels) {
    int currentOffset = verificationTypeInfoOffset;
    int tag = b[currentOffset++] & 0xFF;
    switch (tag) {
        case Frame.ITEM_TOP:
            frame[index] = Opcodes.TOP;
            break;
        case Frame.ITEM_INTEGER:
            frame[index] = Opcodes.INTEGER;
            break;
        case Frame.ITEM_FLOAT:
            frame[index] = Opcodes.FLOAT;
            break;
        case Frame.ITEM_DOUBLE:
            frame[index] = Opcodes.DOUBLE;
            break;
        case Frame.ITEM_LONG:
            frame[index] = Opcodes.LONG;
            break;
        case Frame.ITEM_NULL:
            frame[index] = Opcodes.NULL;
            break;
        case Frame.ITEM_UNINITIALIZED_THIS:
            frame[index] = Opcodes.UNINITIALIZED_THIS;
            break;
        case Frame.ITEM_OBJECT:
            frame[index] = readClass(currentOffset, charBuffer);
            currentOffset += 2;
            break;
        case Frame.ITEM_UNINITIALIZED:
            frame[index] = createLabel(readUnsignedShort(currentOffset), labels);
            currentOffset += 2;
            break;
        default:
            throw new IllegalArgumentException();
    }
    return currentOffset;
}
```

private void appendDescriptor(final StringBuilder stringBuilder) {
    if (sort == OBJECT) {
        stringBuilder.append(valueBuffer, valueBegin - 1, valueEnd + 1);
    } else if (sort == INTERNAL) {
        stringBuilder.append(' ').append(valueBuffer, valueBegin, valueEnd).append(' ');

        stringBuilder.append(valueBuffer, valueBegin, valueEnd);
    }
}

 * Commits or rolls back the transaction based on the provided flag.
